The New R36 Nissan GT-R Is Finally Here, Albeit Only in Spirit – Rendering
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | paolomariagaravaglia
It’s been more than a year since the R35 Nissan GT-R was put to sleep, but the model will return to the automotive world with an entirely new generation, and when it does, it should dwarf its predecessor in all aspects.
Rumor has it that the next generation should come out of hiding officially before the turn of the decade, perhaps the odd one, though some believe that it might actually be a couple of years away from being unveiled. This is contradictory data, and to be honest, it’s not exactly a surprise, because the Japanese company wants to keep most things about this model a secret until the big day comes.
Initial rumors spoke about an all-electric future for the upcoming Nissan GT-R . Needless to say that fans weren’t too happy about it, and since the automaker still listens to its customers, not to mention the fact that the EV market is experiencing a quite sharp divergence by region, has made the automaker reconsider this plan. Thus, ladies and gents, the R36 will not go down the zero-emission route.
A report dating back to six months ago revealed that the model will indeed avoid the EV route completely, as it will still feature an internal combustion lump. Chances are we are looking at a V6 of some sort, perhaps with twin turbocharging. And in order to keep the emissions in check and make the powertrain punchy, it might be assisted by electric trickery, either in the form of a self-charging hybrid or maybe a plug-in hybrid, though we’d lean on the former rather than the latter at this point.
Photo: Instagram | paolomariagaravaglia This recipe should be just about right for a modern-day sports car that will also target the new-age supercar segment in its top form(s), and fans should be happy that the next-generation Nissan GT-R won’t become an EV . Unless they actually dig zero-emission cars, of course. But what about the design part? Well, chances are it might borrow some styling cues from the Nissan Hyper Force Concept .
You do remember the study unveiled roughly three years ago, don’t you? It pretty much looked like a Nissan GT-R from the future, at least toward the rear, because the front fascia was kind of quirky. It featured a very sharp-looking bumper, had a canopy-like design, albeit without the canopy, obviously, cameras instead of side mirrors, an evolution of the R35’s taillights, a large rear wing, and a very aggressive diffuser. And it definitely sent Bosozoku vibes.
Quite strangely, the car manufacturer hasn’t gone into specifics when it comes to the powertrain, but it did announce that the Nissan Hyper Force Concept featured a solid-state battery that feeds electrons to an electric setup. The assembly can generate up to one megawatt of power in total, and this equals 1,340 brake horsepower (1,360 ps).
The study featured a lot of carbon fiber in its body, had a lightweight construction, produced tons of downforce, and had electric all-wheel drive. And while it did look like a Nissan GT-R from the future, from certain angles anyway, not everyone was a fan of the overall design. But worry not, fellow gearhead, because the final production model will definitely be toned down a lot.
Photo: Instagram | paolomariagaravaglia Could it look like the vehicle pictured in the gallery? Well, first things first, this thing came from @paolomariagaravaglia on Instagram, and it is deemed as an R36 Nissan GT-R Concept. And second and more importantly, the answer to this question is likely no. After all, no one who is not directly involve in its development knows anything about it, and this also includes the design.
The car in question kind of looks like a Nissan GT-R , though due to the overall proportions, it seems to be on the quite small side of things. Moreover, due to some of the styling cues, it reminds us of other models from different brands, and here, we’d say Audi and Peugeot. The front fascia does not really do justice to the iconic GT-R nameplate, and to be honest, neither does the profile.
The only things that somewhat reminds us of the R35 are the taillights, and perhaps the rear pillars, and the rear bumper seems to have been inspired by the R8, whereas the roof sends some TT vibes when looking at it from the front. As for the face, it could easily be mistaken for a Peugeot with a few styling tweaks. The wheels were somewhat inspired by the ones equipping the above-mentioned study, with an obvious emphasis on the word “somewhat.”
We (or I in this case) hope that this virtual concept does not end up influencing the actual car in any way, because the upcoming R36 Nissan GT-R has some very big shoes to fill, and this one just does not tick that box. Nevertheless, that does not make it an interesting CGI project, and that’s why we decided to share it with you. But do you actually like the design?
